newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FORECAST-Swedish Riksbank not to cut repo rate.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Swedish Riksbank not to cut repo rate.

text.p: Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, was expected to leave its key interest rate, the repo rate, unchanged at 4.10 percent at its regular weekly tender on Tuesday, a Reuters poll of 12 economists found on Monday.
All the economists surveyed expected no change at the 0830 GMT operation even though there was room for lowering the repo rate, the bank's key tool for controlling money market liquidity.
"There will be no changes, partly on the grounds that there were no essential changes since the last one, partly due to the weak crown," said one of the economists.
The Trade Currency Weighted (TCW) index stood on Monday afternoon at 119.75 which was a bit higher than the Riksbank's desired level for the index.
The Riksbank has said the TCW-index, which indicates the strength of the crown against a weighted basket of currencies, should not be higher than 118.
Some of the economists said the Riksbank apparently wanted to wait until the Consumer Price Index for January was released, on February 20, before making a decision to lower the repo rate again.
"If the CPI data is as good as I expect they will cut the repo rate, depending on if the crown strengthens," said Marie Giertz, Handelsbanken economist.

If the figures show that inflation continurd low or even non-existent then economists expected the Riksbank to lower the repo rate in the longer term. In 1996 the repo was cut 25 times to 4.10 percent from 8.91 percent.
Economists said wage negotiations were also in the spotlight.
"I think it will be unchanged on Tuesday. A further lowering is totally dependent on the crown and on wage negotiations," said John Eriksen, eeconomist at IDEA in London.

Economists interviewed for the poll were from Aragon, Carnegie, Consensus, Den Danske Bank, Hagstromer & Qviberg, Handelsbanken, IDEA, J P Morgan, Merrill Lynch, Nomura, Nordbanken, and Ohman Fondkommission.
